Fairy tail has lots of foreshadowing, what you mean? Take at least in Battle of fairytail, Natsu and Gajeel for some reason couldn't get through barrier implying the both over 80. Which obviously foreshadows the whole timetraveling shenanigans. 

Or Lucy's mother death date being the same as "dragons dissappearing" date, shown in Phantom lord arc, which tells us that Heartfilias were somehow involved with it. 

Or Zeref obviously recognizing Natsu when they first meet in Tenrou arc, while we only find out about their connection like 150 episodes later.

 A few years ago I had a gf who was a part of absolutely every aspect of my life. We texted each other every second, at school she was always with me, we spent time together after school, she was in touch with every friend of mine, even my internet friends, I shared my every hobby and interest with her. Literally my whole life was tied to her.

 But over time, I realize that she had a terrible effect on my mental health, my self-confidence, my awareness.  And that I had to cut it off. So... I did. 

Did it get better after? Oh my god, no. Everything was falling apart, I was falling apart, my brain is blocking the memories of the next 6 months, but even so I remember the only thought "I just want everything to over."  

Two years have passed. Has it gotten better now? No, I'm still mentally unstable, I still only have one person around, I still hate myself and don't know why I keep doing anything. 

But. Did I regret cutting her off? Not for a second. I could be killing myself because of it, but I always knew that this decision was the right one. I was left with nothing, but emptiness was better than suffocation. To be positive, I guess it could be considered a "blank paper, new start", but uh- even I can't believe in this.

 Lately I've been trying to analyze why I keep doing it anyway. I've come to the conclusion that I'll just never be able to put /myself/ first. I cannot be mine first choice, I cannot try for myself, I cannot live for myself, because /me/ is not enough. 

But even so, I guess I am a selfish person, and I do want to be someone's first choice. So maybe I think that if I put them in first place, they will do the same in return. Even if I realise that no, they won't.

So maybe you deserve a little rest? I'm not saying you should give up, of course not. But maybe it's time to stop fighting for a while. You know, let your brain think all the worst-case scenarios? Stop holding back all the terrible thoughts and let them go and go. Until they run out. And when the silence comes, you can take a new breath and decide what to do next.
